artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth complex projective variety. The tangent bundle T_X is said to be pseudo-effective if either (equivalently) (i) there exists an ample line bundle A on X such that A ⊗ Sym^m(T_X) is generically globally generated for every integer m > 0, or (ii) the non-nef locus of the tautological line bundle O_{P(T_X)}(1) on the projectivized tangent bundle P(T_X) is not dominant over X.

It is known that for such X there exists a holomorphic maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration φ : X → Y onto a smooth projective variety Y, i.e. a surjective morphism with connected fibers whose general fiber is rationally connected and such that Y is not uniruled (in fact, satisfies the appropriate properties of an MRC quotient).

Question: For every smooth projective variety X with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, is the holomorphic MRC fibration φ : X → Y locally trivial in the analytic (or étale) topology, that is, does every point y ∈ Y admit an open neighborhood U such that φ^{-1}(U) ≅ U × F, where F is the fiber of φ?
artifact.category_tag: Pseudo-effective tangent bundles and MRC fibrations
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on positivity of tangent sheaves treats the local triviality of the MRC fibration in the pseudo-effective (and almost nef) case as an expectation/conjecture rather than a theorem. Local constancy is known under stronger positivity hypotheses, but the pseudo-effective case appears still open.

status_evidence.snippet: the fibration α:X→Y is not necessarily locally constant, but it is expected to be locally trivial
status_evidence.claim: Local triviality of the MRC fibration is stated as an expectation/conjecture, indicating the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: On projective manifolds with pseudo-effective tangent bundle
status_evidence.snippet: Structure theorem: X admits a holomorphic MRC fibration to a smooth projective variety Y.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes existence of the holomorphic MRC fibration but does not prove local triviality.
